title: Power Budget Calculator
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: A year-long day-by-day battery state-of-charge simulation starting in March, with an itemised daily load, the 0.7 panel loss factor shown as a separate step, temperature derating, a bad-week stress test and a pass or fail verdict naming the month of failure.

learningObjectives: Judge whether a panel, battery and duty cycle will survive the worst month.
Justify a design against a simulated year rather than an average day.
Quantify how much of a fix comes from software rather than hardware.
Explain why cold weather attacks both solar input and battery capacity.
prerequisites: Chapter 16: power budgets, solar sizing, autonomy and duty cycling

keyQuestions: Why does a station built in May fail in November?
Does a bigger battery fix an energy deficit?
What is the cheapest change that keeps this station alive?
commonMisconceptions: A design that works in summer will work all year.
A bigger battery solves a power shortfall.
Sizing the panel is a hardware problem only.
Battery capacity is the same in winter as in summer.
assessmentOpportunities: Names the month a default design fails and explains why spring testing misses it.
Records the saving from each duty-cycle measure and its cost.
Specifies a configuration that survives a bad week in the worst month.
